title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
A digitally coloured scanning electron micrograph of barbed defensive trichomes on the underside of a desert stingbush leaf (Eucnide urens, Loasaceae) (Credit: Rosemary Glos and Carol Flegler)

This month’s cover image is provided by the authors of Glos et al.’s ‘Separate and synergistic anti-herbivore effects of non-glandular trichomes and leaf chemistry in a desert plant’ (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70248), which features in this issue. They experimentally tested the separate and combined effects of two common plant defences, non-glandular trichomes and leaf metabolites, on the feeding, behaviour and performance of beet armyworm caterpillars. Their results indicate that plant defences can synergistically reduce herbivore performance. These findings provide a rare example of trait synergy as a defence strategy and represent a step forward in the effort to study plant defence holistically, as suites or syndromes of defences, rather than isolated traits.
